subject: Follow-up: Demo and removal scenarios checklist for FinApps
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: Demo and removal scenarios checklist for FinApps

Hi Elena / Marco —

Thanks again for your time this morning — appreciate the deep dive into FinApps' ingestion and retention constraints. Per your ask, putting a short, concrete checklist here so we can align on the deletion/RTBF paths and any constraints from your compliance team. I’ve looped in Marissa (AE) and Ben (Solutions) for procurement and technical follow-up.

High-level items we discussed:
- Scenario A: Account-level purge after contract termination (all derived artifacts + embeddings).
- Scenario B: User-initiated delete (individual user or dataset) with audit trail.
- Scenario C: Legal hold / eDiscovery exceptions and how we pause purge.

Questions we still need to confirm from FinApps:
1) Which objects must be removed for Scenario A (raw uploads, parsed text, embeddings, logs)?
2) Maximum acceptable purge timeline (e.g., immediate, 24h, 7 days).
3) Acceptance of deletion proofs: logs, signed attestations, or redacted sample outputs?
4) Residency constraints for backups — can we delete cloud backups or are they managed by a separate retention policy?

Next steps I propose:
- FinApps to confirm answers above by EOD Wed (11/11).
- Redwood to share a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) with timelines and evidence types — I’ll include a draft playbook + a simple data-flow diagram (attached).
- If needed, schedule 30 min with Rishi from our security team for specifics on backups/logs.

Attachments: data-flow-diagram.png (visual of where data and caches live).

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Demo and removal scenarios checklist for FinApps

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the recap and the diagram — that helped. Quick answers and clarifications from our side:

About objects to remove:
- Primary requirement: permanently remove any PII-containing artifacts derived from FinApps users (parsed excerpts, embeddings, vector indexes containing user content).
- Secondary: we can accept retaining anonymized telemetry if it is aggregated and does not contain user identifiers.

Timelines:
- For individual user delete requests: we need confirmation of deletion within 72 hours for our customers; evidence within 7 days.
- For account-level purge on contract termination: acceptable window is 14 days to finalize internal deprovisioning, but we need a mechanism to start immediate purge on our trigger if a legal requirement arises.

Backups / immutable snapshots:
- We run nightly backups in a separate object store (S3 with versioning) and a 90-day retention policy managed by our infra team. We want to understand whether Redwood can:
  a) delete objects that are present in those backups on request, or
  b) provide compensating controls and a documented hold/rewrite process if backups cannot be mutated.

Proof of deletion:
- Audit logs or signed attestations are preferred. A redacted sample is acceptable for initial review but we will need machine-readable logs for compliance.

Can you have Rishi join a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through how Redwood handles immutable backups and log retention? Also, please share the MAP you mentioned.

Best,
Elena
Director of Compliance | FinApps
elena.rossi@finapps.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:18:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Demo and removal scenarios checklist for FinApps

Olga / Marissa —

Looping in high-level answers from security/ops so you can relay to FinApps. Happy to join the call tomorrow — I’ve penciled in 10:00am CET unless you tell me otherwise.

Key points (tech/ops summary):
- Data model: customer content flows through ingestion -> transient parsing layer -> model runtime (KV cache) -> persistent stores (vector index + object store). We also emit request-level logs and aggregation telemetry.

Deletion semantics by object type:
- Object store (raw uploads / parsed text): we can delete objects immediately when requested. Deletion is a tombstone + eventual GC; for S3-like stores we mark for deletion and purge within our GC window (configurable, default 24–48h).
- Vector indexes / embeddings: we support per-customer index deletion. Deletion triggers async rebuild and compaction; in most cases tokens referencing deleted docs are removed within 72h; we can accelerate to 24h for SLA commits with reserved capacity.
- KV cache / runtime caches: ephemeral and cleared on request; no backups.
- Logs: request logs are stored for 30 days by default; we can offer shortened windows (e.g., 7 days) under contract but must discuss trade-offs for debugging.

Backups and immutable snapshots:
- Immutable nightly backups are written to a separate backup bucket with object versioning. By design, these cannot be mutated in-place. Options we offer:
  1) Erasure-in-place via rewriting backup objects: we can run a rewrite job to replace objects with zero-length placeholders or remove versions, then reindex — this is operationally intensive and has a cost/time delta. Typical completion for a single-account rewrite across a 90-day backup set is 7–14 days, dependent on data volume.
  2) Compensating control: keep backups intact but mark the account as terminated and encrypt backup objects with a per-customer KMS key we then destroy (crypto-erase). This achieves practical unreadability but some auditors prefer explicit object deletion.

Proof of deletion / evidence:
- We can provide machine-readable audit logs containing deletion events (object keys, timestamps, operator IDs) plus a signed attestation PDF. For backups rewritten we supply job run logs and checksums.

Suggested MAP items to propose to FinApps:
- Confirmed targets for Scenario A/B/C (explicit object types).
- SLA options: Standard (72h index purge, 14d backup rewrite) vs Accelerated (24h index purge, 7d backup rewrite for a fee).
- Evidence package: machine-readable logs + signed attestation within agreed window.

Attachments I’m adding for internal use: proposed-m-a-p.csv (simple action plan + owners), SLA-redlines.pdf (security-side constraints).

Happy to clean these into a customer-facing MAP once FinApps confirms object list.

–Rishi
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Elena / Marco —

Proposed mutual action plan (draft):
- FinApps to confirm object types for Scenario A by EOD Thu (11/12).
- Redwood to commit to Standard SLA: index purge within 72h, backup rewrite within 14 days. Alternate Accelerated SLA available for an additional commitment (details in attached MAP).
- Redwood to provide machine-readable deletion logs and a signed attestation PDF within 7 days of purge completion.
- Schedule 30-min call: Rishi to walk backups/rewrite options tomorrow at 10:00am CET (proposed).

Deliverables attached: data-flow-diagram.png, proposed-m-a-p.csv, SLA-redlines.pdf.

Please confirm the MAP and whether FinApps prefers Standard or Accelerated SLA for the pilot so we can include it in the SOW. If you want us to reword the attestation to include specific fields for your compliance team, indicate the required fields and we’ll update.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up and getting you onto a pilot cluster.
